A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, with all twelve original plots matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original analyses of language and vision representations in Figures 1–4, plus Gaussian simulations and supplementary analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds CLIP representation comparisons in Appendix J and Figure 13.

M1.justification: The conditional-rank information-imbalance procedure, activation binarization, Hamming distances, and multi-token representations remain unchanged. The expanded estimator equation and revised aggregation advice do not establish a change in the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same opus_books language pairs, ImageNet1k image pairs, Flickr30k image-caption pairs, and Gaussian simulations. The added CLIP comparisons use existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds CLIP image and text encoders to reported comparisons with DinoV2 and DeepSeek-V3 in Figure 13. The previous language-model, vision-model, and neighborhood-overlap comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V1 specifies 40–50 tokens for one sentence and 40–80 for its translation; v2 states 40–80 for the filtered pairs and short-sentence experiments. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence that the unchanged plots were recomputed. Figure 13 also introduces CLIP depth sweeps with specified fixed source layers.

E4.justification: Appendix J adds comparisons probing how CLIP's joint image-text training relates to visual, textual, and cross-modal alignment. Existing token-window, averaging, shuffling, binarization, neighborhood-overlap, and intrinsic-dimension analyses are retained across appendix renumbering.

E5.justification: The new CLIP results explicitly report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals in Figure 13, extending the existing standard-deviation and one-sigma reporting. Repetition counts and uncertainty procedures for the retained results are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 13 adds bidirectional CLIP alignment curves, including a DeepSeek-V3-to-CLIP-Image minimum near 0.3. The previously reported DeepSeek-V3-to-DinoV2 minimum near 0.4 and the plotted results in Figures 1–12 are retained. These are additional model comparisons, not improvements for an unchanged model pairing.

T1.justification: Equation 1 adds a sample-mean expansion of the existing conditional-rank expectation, explaining the existing metric. The asymmetry definition, binary intrinsic-dimension ansatz, and formal properties remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the causal-asymmetry contribution to DeepSeek-V3 processing English and removes directional information flow as a quality indicator from the conclusion. The central claims about semantic layers, distributed information, and language-vision alignment remain.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the asserted asymmetry–quality relationship with language heterogeneity and an open research question, and adds interpretations of CLIP's joint training. It recommends concatenating roughly 20 text tokens instead of averaging 10–20 and emphasizes 200 image tokens where v1 emphasized benefits from 50. The explicit limitation on applying the method to a single sentence pair is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds CLIP configuration details, a DeepSeek-V3 asset link, and a promise to release code upon acceptance; it does not supply that code. It removes the explanation of loading all layers once and Figure 3's specification that averaging uses the ten largest token distances.

R1.justification: V2 adds the CLIP paper by Radford et al., bringing the references from 41 to 42 while retaining all previous works. It also describes the Platonic representation hypothesis as convergence toward similar rather than identical representations; the broader positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The title and Section 2 are renamed, subsection 3.1.5 is merged into 3.1.4, and translation preprocessing moves to Appendix D. Selected passages are rewritten, ethics and reproducibility statements are added, and acknowledgments are removed. The overall narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds the three-panel Figure 13, resizes several appendix plots, including Figures 5 and 6, and relocates figures through text reflow. Existing Figures 1–12 retain their plotted content, with limited caption and layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 better matches its claims to the unchanged Figure 3 evidence by withdrawing the broad causal-asymmetry quality claim. The CLIP comparisons and confidence intervals add useful evidence for the multimodal analysis. These limited gains outweigh losses in documentation precision, particularly the omitted averaging range and explicit single-pair applicability limitation.
